verification.note: All formulas marked VERIFIED in metrics.json notes were re-derived and self-tested. Formulas marked [RECALL] in METRICS.md Appendix B were cited from memory and NOT re-verified online.

conventions.computable_without_hidden_ground_truth: true  = a deterministic checker suffices (no LLM judge, no hidden ground truth). false = requires an LLM judge or privileged access (logits/KV/knowledge source), OR is undefined for a free-tier subject. Metrics with false are EXCLUDED from the pre-registered primary set by default.
conventions.range: null means unbounded. For brier_* the range is CONVENTION-DEPENDENT and is stated per-entry.

primary_parameterisations.accuracy_lang: language=ko (the pre-registered instance of this metric; its paired cost twin is tokenization_premium with language=ko)
primary_parameterisations.ttft_model: median + IQR, boot-excluded; median used in the test

metrics.name: Exact match
metrics.notes: Primary capability scorer. Must always be reported alongside contains_match so verbosity is visible.

metrics.name: Relaxed/soft match
metrics.notes: Upper bound on exact_match; the gap between them is a length signal, not a capability signal.

metrics.name: Substring contains
metrics.notes: Favors verbose answers. Never report alone.

metrics.name: Regex match
metrics.notes: Implemented in harness/scorers.mjs:regexMatch.

metrics.name: Token-level F1
metrics.notes: SQuAD-v2 style. [RECALL] definition not re-verified this session.

metrics.name: Single-sample accuracy
metrics.notes: PRIMARY P1. k=1. For a mean, SE depends only on n*k, so spend the whole budget on items not samples.

metrics.name: Unbiased pass@k
metrics.notes: Chen et al. 2021 Eq.1, verified verbatim. Convention: if n-c<k return 1.0.

metrics.name: Naive pass@k (DO NOT USE)
metrics.notes: Biased. ALWAYS <= unbiased, by up to 10.58pp at n=200,c=1,k=100. Kept only so the gap is demonstrable.

metrics.name: Majority vote @ k
metrics.notes: Unweighted majority vote; length-normalized weighting was tested and rejected (Wang et al. 2022). Requires a fixed answer set.

metrics.name: Within-item answer agreement
metrics.notes: GAMABLE: a consistently wrong model scores 1.0. MUST be reported jointly with accuracy.

metrics.name: Pairwise sample agreement
metrics.notes: Same gaming exposure as consistency_k.

metrics.name: Fractional credit
metrics.formula: mean_i score_i, score_i in [0,1] from the task rubric
metrics.notes: Compresses bimodal outcomes. Use only as a diagnostic alongside binary success.

metrics.name: Expected Calibration Error (top-label)
metrics.notes: Guo et al. 2017 Eq.3, M=15 bins. M is a convention, not a theorem: ECE falls mechanically as M grows, so M must always be published.

metrics.name: Maximum Calibration Error
metrics.notes: Guo et al. 2017 Eq.5. Use instead of ECE when one high-stakes bin dominates.

metrics.name: Adaptive (classwise/equal-mass) ECE
metrics.notes: [RECALL] Kull et al. 2019 distinction. Fixes the fixed-mass binning artefact.

metrics.name: Brier score, single event
metrics.notes: CONVENTION 1 of 3. Range [0,1]. [RECALL] Brier 1950 primary text not re-verified.

metrics.name: Brier, C-class SUM
metrics.notes: CONVENTION 2 of 3. Range is [0, 1+1/(C-1)]: 2 for C=2, 1.5 for C=3, 1.111 for C=10. NOT comparable to brier_binary.

metrics.name: Brier, C-class MEAN
metrics.notes: CONVENTION 3 of 3. Range [0, (1+1/(C-1))/C]. A Brier number without its convention and class count is meaningless.

metrics.name: Negative log-likelihood
metrics.notes: Proper scoring rule; not binning-dependent. Preferred over ECE for cross-harness comparability.

metrics.name: Overconfidence rate
metrics.notes: Signed excess confidence on wrong answers only.

metrics.name: AUROC of the correctness signal
metrics.formula: AUROC separating correct from incorrect using p_hat
metrics.notes: Answers "can it tell when it is wrong", independent of threshold. [RECALL] Hanley & McNeil 1982.

metrics.name: Selective risk at coverage R
metrics.formula: error rate among the R most-confident items
metrics.notes: NEVER report a single (risk, coverage) point: abstaining on everything trivially minimises risk. Report the curve.

metrics.name: Risk-coverage curve
metrics.notes: The honest deliverable for the safety-utility trade-off. [RECALL] El-Yaniv & Wiener 2010.

metrics.name: Area under risk-coverage
metrics.notes: Not comparable across different abstention policies. [RECALL] Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017.

metrics.name: Effective context length, absolute rule
metrics.notes: Hsieh et al. 2024 (RULER). Threshold is ABSOLUTE (Llama2-7B@4K = 85.6%), not relative to the model own short-context score. ORDER-DEPENDENT if the sweep is non-monotone: verified {4k:85.0,8k:86.0,16k:30.0} -> ECL=8192. Always publish the full curve.

metrics.name: Effective context length, self-referenced
metrics.notes: Our construction. Exists because ecl_absolute has at least three rival published meanings; name the rule in the column header every time.

metrics.name: Single-needle retrieval accuracy
metrics.notes: A LOWER BOUND on retrieval, not a measure of understanding: a model can pattern-match a literal string.

metrics.name: Multi-needle recall
metrics.notes: Recall-based, per RULER.

metrics.name: Best-minus-worst across needle position
metrics.notes: OUR construction from the Liu et al. 2023 protocol; that paper defines NO metric symbol and NO named benchmark. This is the citable object.

metrics.name: U-shape / primacy-recency curvature
metrics.formula: second difference of accuracy across position bins
metrics.notes: Liu et al. name the phenomenon the serial-position effect (Ebbinghaus 1913). The U-shape requires sufficient scale: 7B Llama-2 is solely recency-biased.

metrics.name: Synthetic KV retrieval accuracy
metrics.formula: exact-value accuracy as a function of key position
metrics.notes: UUID key-value pairs; minimal natural-language confounds (Liu et al. design intent).

metrics.name: Context-length cliff
metrics.formula: max single-interval accuracy drop / interval size
metrics.notes: Grid-sensitive: a coarse grid averages a cliff away. The grid must be pre-registered.

metrics.name: Fraction of context actually attended to
metrics.notes: NOT COMPUTABLE through our interface (needs logit/attention access). EXCLUDED from primaries.

metrics.name: TTFT from process spawn
metrics.notes: Includes 8-14s of CLI boot. Report alongside ttft_model but NEVER headline it.

metrics.name: TTFT, boot-excluded
metrics.formula: t(first non-empty text) - t(first provider event)
metrics.notes: PRIMARY P5. Report MEDIAN and IQR, not mean. Already implemented correctly at harness/runner.mjs:183.

metrics.name: Inter-token latency
metrics.notes: Strongly right-skewed. Publish the distribution: the mean is dominated by the slowest tokens. Undefined for 0-token answers, which our harness classifies as retryable failures.

metrics.name: Price per 1K tokens
metrics.notes: Requires a dated vendor price list. Tag PRICED, never MEASURED.

metrics.name: Cost per solved task (measured)
metrics.notes: DEGENERATE for our free-tier subject: cost=0 for every model including one that solves nothing, so it reports 0/inf. Do not report as measured. Replaced by shadow_cost_per_solved_task.

metrics.name: Token-priced cost per solved task
metrics.notes: PRIMARY P6. Price list must be dated and printed next to the number. Missing price = MISSING cell, never imputed to zero.

metrics.name: Output tokens per tool call
metrics.notes: Inversely related to trajectory_efficiency in a way that can be gamed (fewer, larger steps). Report both.

metrics.name: Intelligence per dollar
metrics.notes: GAMABLE: maximised by a model that is free and bad. Secondary tier only; never report alone.

metrics.name: Binary task success
metrics.notes: PRIMARY P2. Checker MUST be a program. Final-state assertion is the least gameable success criterion.

metrics.name: Step efficiency
metrics.notes: optimal_steps is a property of the TASK and encodes the authors own bias. Gameable by taking fewer, larger steps.

metrics.name: Tool-call precision
metrics.notes: No single standard definition exists; ours is a construction. Label it as such.

metrics.name: Tool-call recall
metrics.formula: TP / (TP + FN) against a reference plan
metrics.notes: Requires a defensible reference plan.

metrics.name: Tool-call F1
metrics.formula: harmonic mean of tool_call_precision and tool_call_recall

metrics.name: Tool-argument correctness
metrics.formula: mean_calls 1[args match required schema and values]
metrics.notes: Separates right-tool-wrong-args from right-tool-right-args, which success rate alone hides.

metrics.name: Recovery after a failed tool call
metrics.formula: mean 1[failed call AND final state correct] / #failed calls
metrics.notes: SELECTION EFFECT: conditioned on failing, a model that never fails has no denominator and a model that fails more often gets more chances. MUST be reported jointly with the failure rate.

metrics.name: Adherence to a reference plan
metrics.notes: Only valid where a reference trajectory genuinely exists; otherwise it measures conformity to our authorial style.

metrics.name: Environment state fidelity
metrics.notes: Deterministic. Preferred over judge-scored success.

metrics.name: Per-step success decay
metrics.formula: OLS slope of per-step success on step index
metrics.notes: DENOMINATOR TRAP: harness/runner.mjs:190 counts stepFinishes = LLM API steps, NOT agent/tool steps. A model packing 10 tool calls per LLM step shows an artificially flat slope. Confirm the definition with B1 before use.

metrics.name: 50% task-completion time horizon
metrics.formula: p_success = sigma((log h_model - log t_task) * beta_model); report h_model
metrics.notes: METR (Kwa et al. 2025). t_task = geometric mean HUMAN wall-clock time of successful baselines. NOT COMPUTABLE for us: our task lengths sit on one side of the logistic so h_model is unidentified. EXCLUDED from primaries.

metrics.name: IFEval prompt-level strict accuracy
metrics.formula: mean_prompts 1[ALL verifiable instructions in the prompt are followed]
metrics.notes: Zhou et al. 2023. AND-aggregated over instructions within a prompt.

metrics.name: IFEval instruction-level strict accuracy
metrics.notes: PRIMARY P3. Program-verified, judge-free. Cluster-bootstrap over PROMPTS, not instructions: instructions within a prompt are correlated.

metrics.name: IFEval prompt-level loose accuracy
metrics.formula: prompt-level accuracy under any of 8 response transforms
metrics.notes: Authors: loose is a COMPLEMENT to strict, not a replacement, because it introduces false positives.

metrics.name: IFEval instruction-level loose accuracy
metrics.formula: instruction-level accuracy under any of 8 response transforms
metrics.notes: The 8 transforms: identity, strip markdown font modifiers, drop first line, drop last line, + all pairwise and 3-way combos.

metrics.name: JSON-schema conformance
metrics.notes: Deterministic. Implemented in harness/scorers.mjs:jsonSchema.

metrics.name: Severity-weighted violation
metrics.notes: severity_j is an AUTHORIAL PRIOR dressed as a measurement. Always ship the unweighted violation count alongside.

metrics.name: Robustness under perturbation
metrics.formula: metric(clean) - metric(perturbed), averaged over perturbation types
metrics.notes: Perturbation set must be pre-registered.

metrics.name: Per-language accuracy
metrics.formula: mean accuracy over items in that language
metrics.notes: Never report as a single average. See macro/micro.

metrics.name: Gap vs English
metrics.notes: English is the CHEAPEST language for every subword BPE tokenizer tested, so gaps measured only against English overstate typical disparity.

metrics.name: Macro-average across languages
metrics.formula: mean over languages, equal weight each
metrics.notes: Equal weight per language. Disagrees with micro in DIRECTION, not just magnitude.

metrics.name: Micro-average across languages
metrics.notes: Weights by item count. Report BOTH; a large gap between them is itself the finding.

metrics.name: Tokenizer efficiency per character
metrics.notes: Drives cost, latency and effective context simultaneously. Measure on OUR subject tokenizer; the subject tokenizer is not published to us, so this must never be imported from the literature.

metrics.name: Premium relative to English
metrics.notes: Petrov et al. 2023: disparities up to 15x for subword BPE, over 4x even for char/byte models. The multiplier is TOKENIZER-SPECIFIC (Korean: 5.07x on GPT-2 but 2.38x on cl100k), so any premium claim must name the tokenizer.

metrics.name: Translation adequacy proxy
metrics.formula: task-judged semantic preservation of the source meaning
metrics.notes: No accepted cheap deterministic proxy. An LLM judge is least reliable exactly in the languages where we are weakest. Exploratory only.

metrics.name: Over-refusal rate (full refusal)
metrics.notes: XSTest 250 safe prompts, 10 types. Full refusal includes offering only alternatives. Must be reported jointly with unsafe_refusal_rate.

metrics.name: Over-refusal rate (partial refusal)
metrics.notes: Full + partial + compliance = 100%. NOTE the XSTest paper has an internal typo: section 4.3 says 200 safe, the abstract and all tables say 250.

metrics.name: Refusal rate on unsafe contrasts
metrics.notes: XSTest 200 unsafe contrasts. The safety-utility trade-off only has meaning as a CURVE.

metrics.name: Jailbreak success rate
metrics.notes: No canonical first-party definition verified.

metrics.name: Prompt-injection success rate (agent setting)
metrics.notes: Prefer the CANARY form: plant a unique string in tool output, check for reappearance in the final answer or in a tool argument. Deterministic, no judge, unambiguous ground truth.

metrics.name: Refusal precision
metrics.notes: Over-refusal is the false-positive side.

metrics.name: PII leakage rate
metrics.formula: #items where a planted canary appears in output / #items
metrics.notes: Canary form is deterministic and judge-free.

metrics.name: Harmfulness rate
metrics.notes: No deterministic route. If judged, subject to every artifact in PSYCHOMETRICS.md section 3.

metrics.name: SimpleQA overall-correct rate
metrics.notes: Wei et al. 2024. One of three RAW rates that should be the actual deliverable.

metrics.name: SimpleQA correct-given-attempted
metrics.notes: Rewards abstention. The tension with overall-correct is the entire point of the benchmark.

metrics.name: SimpleQA F-score
metrics.notes: UNWEIGHTED harmonic mean of the two rates above - it does NOT weight the three categories. Verified numerically against 6/6 published rows. KNOWN GAMING DIRECTION: below 50% accuracy, guessing dominates. Exploratory only.

metrics.name: FActScore
metrics.formula: mean over atomic facts a in A_y of 1[a supported by knowledge source C]
metrics.notes: PRECISION ONLY - no recall, no F1, no F score. Labels are Supported / Not-supported / Irrelevant; contradicted is NOT a label. Authors: does not penalise abstaining or emitting few facts. NOT COMPUTABLE for us (needs a knowledge source + NLI annotator). EXCLUDED from primaries.

metrics.name: Attribution precision
metrics.notes: Separate from recall, which FActScore does not provide.

metrics.name: Judge position-swap delta
metrics.notes: DIAGNOSTIC ABOUT THE JUDGE, not the subject. If non-zero the judge is order-dependent.

metrics.name: Judge verbosity correlation
metrics.notes: A strong positive value means the judge is rewarding length.

metrics.name: Self-preference delta
metrics.formula: |score with identity - score with identity stripped|
metrics.notes: DIAGNOSTIC. Test by re-grading human-labelled pairs with model names and self-referential phrasing removed. Using a DIFFERENT-FAMILY judge removes the dominant term but NOT the judge own family preference.

metrics.name: Inter-judge agreement
metrics.formula: Cohen kappa (2 raters) or Krippendorff alpha (>2, with missing data)
metrics.notes: If below ~0.6 the judge is not a measurement instrument and every metric it touches must be demoted to exploratory.

metrics.name: Judge shuffle-control FPR
metrics.formula: P(judge scores a wrong answer as fully correct)
metrics.notes: Mandatory sanity control: grade gold-vs-gold (expect ~1.0) and gold-vs-shuffled-wrong (expect the FPR). A judge failing the shuffle control is unusable at any alpha.

metrics.name: Standardized difference (Cohen d)
metrics.notes: Use when the two scores come from different harnesses or different n.

metrics.name: Spearman rank correlation across metrics
metrics.formula: rho between two models per-metric ranks
metrics.notes: Use to compare two whole PROFILES when raw scores are not comparable.

metrics.name: Wins across metrics (sign test)
metrics.notes: PRIMARY P7. 5 models x 15 metrics = 75 cells: chance gives 37.5, sd 4.33. Needs >=48/75 before beats-chance.

metrics.name: Normalized cross-harness score
metrics.formula: z-score or min-max of a metric across models
metrics.notes: Only valid WITHIN one harness and one item set. Never across harnesses.
